title: Swahili merchants connect the Indian Ocean
summary: Kilwa’s merchants participated in Indian Ocean trade linking the East African coast with Arabia, India and China. Gold, ivory, ceramics and other goods moved through these overlapping commercial networks.

claims.text: Kilwa’s merchants participated in Indian Ocean trade linking the East African coast with Arabia, India and China. Gold, ivory, ceramics and other goods moved through these overlapping commercial networks.
Thirteenth–sixteenth centuries describes the documented trading period, not all occupation.

Trade goods provide evidence of connection beyond mere chronological coincidence. Kilwa should be understood as an active Swahili centre of commerce, with local institutions and architecture, rather than a passive stop on someone else’s route.
